candidate_adjudications.title: Unsafe setattr in conftest.py dynamic module initialization

root_cause_analysis.rationale: Located in tests/conftest.py which is a pytest test fixture configuration file. The loop iterates over a fixed, hardcoded tuple of literal string levels: ('debug', 'info', 'warn', 'warning', 'error'). No attacker-controlled input can reach this function, and the code only executes in the test runner environment. Marking this as an arbitrary attribute injection vulnerability was a static analysis keyword false positive.

_enforce_same_origin is a before_request hook implemented to mitigate GHSA-4pv4-jmfm-phrw. It checks Origin and falls back to Referer against the Host header. It successfully mitigates cross-origin browser requests (including null origins). However, it intentionally permits requests where neither Origin nor Referer is present (lines 320-323) to support CLI tooling. This represents a trust-boundary design trade-off, not a missing control. This directly overlaps with Candidate P3-M3-03 and the /cmd authorization boundary.

candidate_adjudications.title: Missing referer validation on cross-origin requests

root_cause_analysis.rationale: Line 562 is handle_root() handling GET / to serve index.html. GET requests are idempotent and CSRF protection is not applicable. Furthermore, the claim that referer validation is missing across the application is factually incorrect because _enforce_same_origin (line 318) explicitly falls back to checking Referer when Origin is absent. This finding is a duplicate/hallucinated aspect of Candidate P3-M3-02.

While name parameter comes from URL /scripts/load/<name>, lines 1206-1210 explicitly resolve both safe_root = pathlib.Path(ScriptRoot).resolve() and script_path = (safe_root / ...).resolve(), then strictly check if not script_path.is_relative_to(safe_root): bottle.abort(400, 'Invalid script path'). The use of .resolve() combined with is_relative_to() constitutes an effective, cryptographically sound path containment guard in Python 3.9+. Traversal attempts (e.g. ../../etc/passwd) are rejected. The finding is non-exploitable.

candidate_adjudications.title: handle_scripts_load resolves script path relative to ScriptRoot

root_cause_analysis.rationale: Identical candidate to P3-M3-04 from the sequential investigator. Same location, same function, same false claim of path traversal bypass despite the active is_relative_to() guard.

State-changing POST /cmd endpoint accepts flight commands and dispatches them via self.send() with no user authentication or token-based authorization. Shares the identical underlying root cause (missing authentication/authorization invariant) with /script/run (line 1220/1253) and /script/abort (line 1278).

candidate_adjudications.title: Weak Session Token Heap Address Leak via Session.id

root_cause_analysis.rationale: Session.id property returns str(id(self)), exposing the CPython heap memory address of the object as the session token. Heap allocation patterns are non-cryptographic and predictable, allowing session hijacking.

key_findings: The 4 findings reported in Phase 3 Mode 3 are NOT four independent exploitable vulnerabilities.
tests/conftest.py:77 is a test fixture mock with zero attacker control.
The Origin (line 297) and Referer (line 562) findings share one underlying CSRF architecture; line 562 is an idempotent GET view.
handle_scripts_load (line 1193) is non-exploitable due to pathlib.Path.is_relative_to() containment on resolved paths.
/script/run, /script/abort, and /cmd represent a single root cause: missing authorization invariant across command/script execution dispatch.
